note: Status of each step, checked against docs/DIRECTION.md, docs/RUST-TARGETS.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/EMOJI-ROADMAP.md and the merged pull requests. gather.py drops a 'done' or 'done-emu' node to 'review' while its pull requests are open and to 'progress' if one cannot be found, and sets each node's tag (merged, in review, in progress or planned) from gh. 'done-emu' means checked in an emulator or on the host only; nothing here has run on real hardware. A node marked 'review' is built and checked in an emulator or on the host, in a pull request that is not merged. Edges (deps) mean 'this unlocks that'.

milestone.name: First Window
milestone.what: A window drawn by the shared Desk core, moved with a mouse, on DOS (hosted) and on the bare-metal kernel (native). Reached in emulators with scripted input; not with a real mouse or real hardware.

branches.label: Foundations
branches.next: The emoji hands and the skin-tone mechanism, proved on the eight hands already drawn.

branches.label: Hosted track (Desk on DOS)
branches.next: Live input into SHELL.EXE, then the launcher bar and menus; decide whether to retire the C layer and promote rt to a top-level crate.
branches.blocker: Owner decision on retiring the C layer; the mouse path of the shell is unverified.

branches.label: Convergence (shared)
branches.next: Live input into the shell on both tracks, then widgets and menus on the first window's core.
branches.blocker: The app model: nothing decides what an app is, how it is loaded or how it calls the Desk (the anatomy page of the Desk).

branches.label: Native track (own kernel)
branches.next: Live input on the native shell mode; then the executable-format spike (planned after live input); a V86 monitor if FreeDOS needs it.
branches.blocker: Scheduling, paging and system calls are open decisions; no user mode exists in the kernel.

branches.label: Games and apps
branches.next: Nothing to start until the shared core exists; Fizz Episode 2 is the first customer of the shared drivers, which are now built and merged.

nodes.label: Desk
nodes.what: A calm graphical operating system in Rust for 486-class PCs (working name).
nodes.why: The point of all of it.
nodes.evidence: docs/DIRECTION.md (PR #5)

nodes.label: Design system
nodes.what: Palette, HIG, file formats, SDK ABI shape and the Afterglow prototype.
nodes.why: Everything visual and every format follows from it, on both tracks.
nodes.evidence: docs/PALETTE.md, HIG.md, FORMATS.md, SDK.md and design/ on main (Initial Commit)

nodes.label: Repo, CI, doc checks
nodes.what: liminal-hq/desk with tools/check.sh, the ci-dos image and doc and header checks.
nodes.why: Every later claim is checked here.
nodes.evidence: main a4b0d86; CI green on the merge commit of every pull request (#1 to #7)

nodes.label: Desk fonts
nodes.what: Four pixel faces (Square and Round), Desk Fixed DOS, and Desk Sans, Mono and Serif in four styles; .DFN bitmaps.
nodes.why: The Desk's text on DOS and on the native screen; the outline faces for modern systems.
nodes.evidence: PR #1, merged: bun build.ts --check reproducible; OTS, fontTools, FreeType, HarfBuzz in Docker

nodes.label: Emoji, first set
nodes.what: 480 pixel emoji at 16 and 12 px (40 at 8 px), 156 vector, two colour fonts and .DEM files.
nodes.why: The shell's own pictures and Fizz's icons, in the Desk palette.
nodes.evidence: PR #2, merged: bun test, fontTools, OTS, FreeType pixel-exact against .DEM

nodes.label: Gboard request 164 / 244
nodes.what: Every emoji in Gboard's Smileys and emotions panel; 164 of 244 sequences done.
nodes.why: The owner's request; the faces are complete.
nodes.evidence: docs/EMOJI-ROADMAP.md, generated and checked by bun test; merged in PR #2

nodes.label: Skin tones
nodes.what: Five tones per hand by palette substitution, GSUB in the colour fonts, a role byte in .DEM.
nodes.why: 48 of the 80 planned requests are tone families.
nodes.evidence: Design in docs/EMOJI-ROADMAP.md; nothing built

nodes.label: ZWJ sequences
nodes.what: Seven sequences such as 😮‍💨 and ❤️‍🔥, each its own drawing and ligature.
nodes.why: Completes the request.
nodes.evidence: docs/EMOJI-ROADMAP.md; nothing built

nodes.label: More vector emoji
nodes.what: Vector drawings where the geometric kit can draw well.
nodes.why: Beside Desk Sans, Mono and Serif at large sizes.
nodes.evidence: Step 6 of the emoji roadmap

nodes.label: Product name
nodes.what: Desk is a working name; candidates in docs/NAMING.md.
nodes.why: Names the boot image, disk label and repository. Blocks nothing.
nodes.evidence: docs/NAMING.md

nodes.label: Direction and Rust targets
nodes.what: Two tracks behind a HAL; how Rust is built per application space; the std question.
nodes.why: Records the pivot so the repo and the work agree.
nodes.evidence: PR #5, merged: DIRECTION.md and RUST-TARGETS.md. Documents, not measurements.

nodes.label: Toolchain skeleton
nodes.what: Rust no_std core plus a DJGPP C layer as one DESK.EXE, run headless in DOSBox.
nodes.why: Proved Rust on DOS end to end in CI.
nodes.evidence: PR #3, merged: tools/check.sh in ci-dos; DOSBox Staging only

nodes.label: DXE3 modules
nodes.what: Rust apps as .DXE files loaded with dlopen, calling back into the core.
nodes.why: Apps as modules: yes, with limits (LTO required, stack overflow not recoverable).
nodes.evidence: PR #4, merged: 13 scenarios, 200-cycle leak test, docs/S1-DXE3.md

nodes.label: Pure Rust DOS program
nodes.what: No gcc, libc or crt0: rust-lld, a 139-line packer and the rt runtime.
nodes.why: Rust for DOS without the C layer; shared with Fizz Episode 2.
nodes.evidence: PR #7, merged: transcripts, IRQ 0 hook and mode 13h headless, docs/D0-RUST-DOS.md

nodes.label: Retire the C layer
nodes.what: Drop c/, coff2go32.py and DJGPP's libc once the hardware code has moved to Rust.
nodes.why: One toolchain; d0 recommends it.
nodes.evidence: docs/D0-RUST-DOS.md, recommendation

nodes.label: ELF target and rt crate
nodes.what: dos-elf.json as the DOS target; rt promoted to a top-level crate with an exception handler.
nodes.why: The base every DOS program and the hosted Desk build on.
nodes.evidence: docs/D0-RUST-DOS.md, next spikes

nodes.label: VBE and mode 12h
nodes.what: VGA modes 13h and 12h, the DAC and VBE 2.0 with a linear frame buffer (DPMI 0800h), from Rust, proved in DOSBox Staging by read-back checksums.
nodes.why: Pixels for the compositor.
nodes.evidence: docs/A-VGA-VBE.md; PR #11, merged, CI passing on the merge commit. Checked in DOSBox Staging only; no real VGA chip.

nodes.label: Keyboard and mouse
nodes.what: The keyboard on IRQ 1 under DPMI and the mouse through INT 33h by polling, producing the same event types as the native kernel. The real-mode callback was not built.
nodes.why: Input for windows and the cursor.
nodes.evidence: docs/B-DOS-INPUT.md; PR #15, merged, CI passing on the merge commit. DOSBox's own mouse driver only.

nodes.label: OPL and Sound Blaster
nodes.what: OPL music and Sound Blaster DMA from Rust.
nodes.why: Audio Player, Fizz, system sounds.
nodes.evidence: docs/D0-RUST-DOS.md, next spikes

nodes.label: Hosted shell
nodes.what: Compositor, windows, launcher bar, cursor and keyboard focus on DOS. Built so far: two windows with the stepped halo, text, a software cursor and focus, as SHELL.EXE on the pure-Rust runtime.
nodes.why: The first thing anyone would call the Desk.
nodes.evidence: docs/FIRST-WINDOW.md Result; PRs #19 and #30 merged. SHELL.EXE runs in DOSBox against the goldens; the launcher bar, menus and apps are not built, the mouse is not verified, nothing ran on real hardware.

nodes.label: DOS handoff
nodes.what: DESK.COM, DESK.RUN and /RESUME: run a DOS program and come back.
nodes.why: Any DOS program a double-click away.
nodes.evidence: docs/HANDOFF.md; SPEC.md milestone 3

nodes.label: Files, Programs, Settings
nodes.what: The three core apps.
nodes.why: A usable desktop.
nodes.evidence: SPEC.md milestone 4

nodes.label: js-dos browser build
nodes.what: DOS programs in the browser. The spike programs run unchanged in js-dos 8, and the VBE linear frame buffer works there. The Desk itself is not in the browser, because the hosted Desk does not exist yet.
nodes.why: A demo anyone can open.
nodes.evidence: docs/S5-JSDOS.md; PR #13, merged, CI passing on the merge commit (CI does not run the browser check): headless Chromium only.

nodes.label: Real hardware (DOS)
nodes.what: A real 486, EMM386, QEMM and a Windows 9x DOS box.
nodes.why: Emulators pass things real machines reject.
nodes.evidence: No real hardware is in the loop yet

nodes.label: Hardware layer (HAL)
nodes.what: One crate with two edges: the traits and shared types, a mock platform, and three drivers (serial, PIT, PIC) tested on the host. The input and video surfaces were added by the pull requests that followed it.
nodes.why: One Desk core on both tracks; without it they drift apart.
nodes.evidence: docs/HAL.md; PR #8, merged, CI passing on the merge commit. Host tests; the kernel and the DOS runtime use it through the later merged pull requests, in emulators only; nothing runs on real hardware.

nodes.label: Shared drivers crate
nodes.what: Built and merged: serial, PIT, PIC, the 8042 controller, the scancode decoder, VGA modes 13h, 12h and 03h with the DAC, VBE, and the INT 33h mouse. Not started: OPL, Sound Blaster, DMA, IDE and floppy.
nodes.why: Shared by the hosted Desk, the native kernel and Fizz Episode 2.
nodes.evidence: docs/HAL.md; PRs #8, #10, #11, #15, merged, CI passing on each merge commit; host tests and emulators only

nodes.label: Desk core
nodes.what: Compositor, window manager, widgets, palette, fonts, event loop, app host. Built so far: desk-gfx, desk-font, desk-present, desk-ui, desk-wm and desk-shell.
nodes.why: The product, independent of the machine below.
nodes.evidence: docs/FIRST-WINDOW.md; PR #19 merged (stacked PRs #20 to #28 landed through it). Host-tested with golden frames. Not built: widgets beyond a label and a text field, menus, an app host.

nodes.label: std platform layer
nodes.what: A patched std platform layer over the d0 runtime (55 added lines in 12 files and about 340 lines of new files) that makes println!, HashMap, Instant and process::exit work in DOSBox.
nodes.why: Apps are where std pays off.
nodes.evidence: docs/E-STD-STUBS.md; PR #12, merged, CI passing on the merge commit. Checked in DOSBox Staging; an invented OS name alone does not build.

nodes.label: Bundle FreeDOS
nodes.what: Run DOS programs on the native OS by booting FreeDOS or a V86 task.
nodes.why: No need to reimplement DOS.
nodes.evidence: DIRECTION.md: a later milestone; licences to check

nodes.label: Own stub and extender
nodes.what: Replace the DJGPP stub and perhaps CWSDPMI.
nodes.why: The last pieces of the DOS route that are not ours.
nodes.evidence: D0-RUST-DOS.md: research, not planned

nodes.label: Boot sector and loader
nodes.what: 512-byte NASM boot sector; loader with INT 13h, A20, E820, GDT, protected mode.
nodes.why: Our own way onto the machine.
nodes.evidence: PR #6, merged: three loader variants boot in QEMU -cpu 486

nodes.label: Rust kernel skeleton
nodes.what: GDT, IDT and exceptions, PIC, PIT at 100 Hz, frames, heap with alloc, x87, serial and VGA text.
nodes.why: Native milestones 1 and 2.
nodes.evidence: PR #6, merged: transcript match, five fault modes, a hang watchdog

nodes.label: PS/2 keyboard and mouse
nodes.what: The 8042, the scancode set 1 decoder and the IntelliMouse packets as shared drivers, with the kernel's IRQ 1 and IRQ 12 handlers and a lock-free ring.
nodes.why: Input; native milestone 4.
nodes.evidence: docs/C-INPUT.md; PR #10, merged, CI passing on the merge commit: a QEMU run with injected input matches its expected transcript. No real keyboard or mouse.

nodes.label: VGA, VBE, window and cursor
nodes.what: VBE asked in the loader before the switch to protected mode, VGA modes 13h and 12h by registers, a software cursor and a first window, all in QEMU. Leaving a VBE mode without the BIOS works on QEMU's standard card and fails on its Cirrus card.
nodes.why: A frame drawn by the shared compositor; native milestone 3.
nodes.evidence: docs/D-NATIVE-VGA.md; PR #14, merged, CI passing on the merge commit: real QEMU screendumps checked against reference checksums.

nodes.label: Native BIOS path (n3)
nodes.what: A real-mode trampoline gives the protected-mode kernel the BIOS back one call at a time: VBE set and left on three QEMU cards, floppy and LBA reads, the memory map and the clock. V86 mode and paging are design only.
nodes.why: Spike D found that leaving VBE without the BIOS fails on QEMU's Cirrus card.
nodes.evidence: docs/N3-BIOS-PATH.md; PR #17, merged (it was based on #14), CI passing on the merge commit. Emulators only.

nodes.label: Paging and protection
nodes.what: Flat and shared, or per-app address spaces on the 486 MMU.
nodes.why: Decides what a crashed app can damage.
nodes.evidence: DIRECTION.md open question: memory protection

nodes.label: Scheduling model
nodes.what: Cooperative in one address space, or preemptive processes.
nodes.why: Shapes the app ABI and the core's event loop.
nodes.evidence: DIRECTION.md open question: scheduling

nodes.label: Floppy and IDE
nodes.what: BIOS INT 13h in the loader today; own drivers in the kernel later (a decision).
nodes.why: Reading anything after boot.
nodes.evidence: DIRECTION.md native milestone 5

nodes.label: FAT12/16 filesystem
nodes.what: Read the floppy; perhaps a filesystem of our own for the system volume.
nodes.why: Load apps and files; share disks with FreeDOS.
nodes.evidence: DIRECTION.md native milestone 5

nodes.label: Module format and loader
nodes.what: A format both tracks share, with symbol import, per-module state, panic containment, unload.
nodes.why: Apps loaded from disk; native milestone 6.
nodes.evidence: DIRECTION.md; lessons from S1-DXE3.md. The executable-format spike is planned after live input; nothing is built.

nodes.label: App ABI and syscalls
nodes.what: How an app calls the Desk on the native OS.
nodes.why: Native apps and the std platform layer sit on it.
nodes.evidence: RUST-TARGETS.md space (d)

nodes.label: OPL and Sound Blaster
nodes.what: Sound with detection but without DOS or BLASTER.
nodes.why: Native milestone 8.
nodes.evidence: DIRECTION.md native milestone 8

nodes.label: Desk core on native
nodes.what: The shared core on the native HAL: a window and a cursor on bare metal. Built so far: the kernel's `shell` test mode runs the first-window scenario.
nodes.why: The native half of the first milestone; native milestone 7 begins here.
nodes.evidence: docs/FIRST-WINDOW.md Result; PR #29 merged: QEMU's screendumps equal the goldens at depth 8 and depth 4. A test mode, not a desktop: no live input, no apps.

nodes.label: Bochs and 86Box (spike G)
nodes.what: The native image boots unchanged in Bochs 2.7 as a 486 with three BIOSes and in 86Box 6.0 on a 1993 AMIBIOS board, after a loader fix for a BIOS with neither E820 nor E801. v86, the browser emulator, is a later step.
nodes.why: QEMU alone is one opinion.
nodes.evidence: docs/NATIVE-EMULATORS.md; PR #16, merged, CI passing on the merge commit. The emulator runs are not part of CI, which has no Docker. The merged image has not been run on 86Box. No hardware.

nodes.label: A real 486
nodes.what: Boot the floppy on period hardware.
nodes.why: The actual target.
nodes.evidence: No real hardware available yet; the emulators tried are QEMU, Bochs and 86Box

nodes.label: Lt. Fizz Episode 2
nodes.what: A new DOS game as a plain Rust program on the shared runtime and drivers.
nodes.why: The first outside customer of Rust for DOS.
nodes.evidence: RUST-TARGETS.md space (f)

nodes.label: Migrate Episode 1
nodes.what: Move lieutenant-fizz-dos off its C layer onto the shared machinery.
nodes.why: The origin of the approach.
nodes.evidence: RUST-TARGETS.md space (e): a candidate, an idea

nodes.label: Optional apps
nodes.what: Audio Player and Notes first, then Paint, Clock, Calc, Mines, Terminal, Inspector.
nodes.why: The prototype's apps, for real.
nodes.evidence: SPEC.md milestone 5; design/*.dc.html

nodes.label: TrueType in the Desk
nodes.what: Reading TrueType fonts in the Desk (spike s6).
nodes.why: Outline text on the Desk itself.
nodes.evidence: PR #1 docs: a later spike

nodes.label: Live input into the shell
nodes.what: Keys and the mouse reaching the shell through each platform's own input path (QEMU sendkey and mouse_move; DOSBox AUTOTYPE and a real INT 33h mouse).
nodes.why: The first window is moved by scripted events today; this tests the input path, not the pixels.
nodes.evidence: docs/FIRST-WINDOW-PLAN.md T12 (optional); not started

nodes.label: First Window
nodes.what: A window drawn by the shared core and moved with a mouse, hosted on DOS and native.
nodes.why: The first thing a person would see and call the Desk.
nodes.evidence: PR #31 merged: both tracks' frames equal each other and the host goldens, six frames at two depths, with the negative runs failing. Not moved by a real mouse, not run on real hardware, one emulator per track.
